Grammy Award: Album of the Year nominees

podcast.body: Recorded over two years, this album represented U2's attempt to "reapply for the job of the best band in the world" after the misstep of 'Pop'. It marked a return to a "back to basic" approach, eschewing loops and dancey beats, and saw the reunion of producers Brian Eno (absent from 'Pop') and Daniel Lanzwah (who worked on 'The Joshua Tree' and 'Achtung Baby'). Sessions were held in Dublin and the south of France. It sold 12 million copies, becoming their fourth highest-selling album of all time, and earned seven Grammy Awards, effectively putting the band back on a successful path. "the album put you two back on a correct path selling 12 million copies, making it the fourth highest selling you two album of all time. There were seven Grammy Awards."

srcs.episode: The 00's Part 3: The Return of Rock

podcast.body: Released on October 31, 2000, as pop music was peaking, this album garnered "great reviews," sold over 12 million copies, and won 7 Grammy Awards, signaling hope for rock music's revival. "U2's All That You Can't Leave Behind came out as the pop cycle was starting to peak with Brittany, Backstreet Boys and InSync. However, it cut through. It got great reviews, sold over 12 million copies and won 7 Grammy Awards."

podcast.body: This album contained the hit single "Beautiful Day" and "Walk On." U2 won Record of the Year for "Beautiful Day" in 2001 and again for "Walk On" in 2002, the latter being considered overkill as "Walk On" was not a major hit. "You too had won the prize in 2001 for their Big Hit Beautiful Day. And then they won again the following year for Walk On, a single from the same album that didn't even make the Hot 100 and peaked in the middle of Billboard's Rock charts."
